clue.text: Paid footballer's evaluative response?

blocks.note: read as fee'd, given a fee
a back is a defensive footballer

explanation.surface: A well-paid footballer offers his own assessment of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paid' is split playfully as FEE'D, someone who has been given a fee; a back is a defender in football.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedback is the comment or reaction given after someone's performance, a judgement of how well it went.

clue.text: Aggressively promote electrical gadget

blocks.note: first meaning: to push a product or show hard in publicity
second meaning: the pronged fitting that connects an appliance to the mains

explanation.surface: A salesman pushes some new electrical device hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for relentless publicity and a noun for the pronged connector on an appliance cable.

clue.text: Killer taking two donkeys home

blocks.note: an ass is a donkey, so two of them side by side
at home means in

explanation.surface: A murderer leads a pair of donkeys back to his house.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, especially one who kills a prominent person for pay or politics.

clue.text: American soldiers reversed new board outside inn

indicators.note: something reversed is turned to face the other way, so read the soldiers' letters from right to left

blocks.note: GIs are US army soldiers
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: US troops backed into a freshly painted pub board.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub traditionally hangs a painted sign bearing its name above or beside the front door.

clue.text: Subject taught efficiently at first across border

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the two preceding words
lying across something means stretched over it on both sides, so these letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: the opening letters of the two words
a hem is the finished border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A school topic was taught crisply in a lesson spanning a national frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or central idea that a talk, essay or piece of art is about.

clue.text: Some women thus easily go into raptures

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a portion of their letters run on is wanted

blocks.note: found running across the three words

explanation.surface: A remark that certain women get excited at the drop of a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthuse is to speak with great excitement and delight, which is gushing rapture.

clue.text: Roly-poly cook's first husband

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the cook

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
hubby is the informal word for husband

explanation.surface: A plump chef's first spouse is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Roly-poly is an affectionate term for plump and round, which is what chubby also means.

clue.text: Go back on ship, seeing monster

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the little verb is written right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
re means on or concerning
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A sailor returns to his vessel, only to find a monster aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a man-eating giant of fairy tales, so a monster.

clue.text: Everyone rushed outside for a type of vegetable ...

indicators.note: one word standing outside another goes around it, holding it in the middle

blocks.note: to shoot is to dash, so rushed is shot
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody hurries out for a certain vegetable, and the ellipsis leads on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small mild onion, a type of vegetable used widely in cooking.

clue.text: ... consumed in college, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells the solver to go by how the college is pronounced rather than spelt

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English public school, properly Eton College

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the vegetable is eaten at a school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is an elite boarding school near Windsor; its name said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Consumed and eaten are both past participles meaning taken in as food.

clue.text: A mother? He didn't have one

blocks.note: taken as written
a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: Asked about a mother, someone replies that a certain man never had one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a riddle: in Genesis the first man was formed from dust, so had no mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam was created directly by God according to the Bible, the only man without any parent.

clue.text: Voluntary: unusually plain too

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters are arranged in an uncommon way, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something voluntary is described as being remarkably plain as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Optional and voluntary both describe something left to free choice rather than required.

clue.text: Eager to mourn the departed

blocks.note: first meaning: enthusiastic, very willing
second meaning: to wail in lament over a dead person, an Irish custom

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone impatient to grieve; the second sense is the old Irish verb for crying over the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for enthusiastic and also a verb for wailing a lament at a funeral.

clue.text: Cloth worker given NCO's rank

blocks.note: serge is a hard-wearing woollen fabric
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A textile worker is promoted to a non-commissioned officer's grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned officer holds ranks such as corporal and sergeant, the latter being a senior one.

clue.text: Frenzied Italian climbing in another part of Europe, mostly

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the abbreviation reads from bottom to top
mostly means not quite all, so the country loses its final letter
in places the Italian inside the shortened country name

blocks.note: It is the abbreviation for Italian, as in vermouth
France is another European country

explanation.surface: An Italian is climbing a mountain somewhere else in Europe in a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Frantic and frenzied both describe wild, desperate haste or agitation out of control.

clue.text: Follow directions: take legal action

blocks.note: east and north, two compass points
to sue is to bring a lawsuit

explanation.surface: An instruction to obey orders and go to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards as a result, so it means to follow.

clue.text: Entering wager, request dance after this game

indicators.note: the request enters the wager, going inside it
after this places the dance at the end of what has been built so far

blocks.note: a bet is a wager
to ask is to request
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone placing a bet asks for a dance once this game is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Basketball is a team sport, a game played by shooting a ball through a high hoop.

clue.text: Resort of America, not a peninsula

indicators.note: not tells the solver to leave out the following letter from the country
read as re-sort, to sort again, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
one A to drop

explanation.surface: A holiday spot in the USA is said not to be a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimea is a peninsula jutting into the Black Sea, almost entirely surrounded by water.

clue.text: Relaxation one's found in the French river

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so this goes between the other two pieces

blocks.note: le is French for the
one is I, and the apostrophe S supplies the S
the Ure is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: Someone finds relaxation by a river in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time spent at ease, so relaxation away from work.

clue.text: Cry of wonder about Northern Ireland's spirit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cry wraps around the abbreviation

blocks.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
NI is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: An exclamation of amazement concerning the spirit of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie is a spirit of Arabian legend, such as the one in Aladdin's lamp.

clue.text: Unsteady on one's feet? That's astonishing!

blocks.note: first meaning: walking or standing unsteadily, lurching
second meaning: amazing, so surprising it knocks you back

explanation.surface: Someone tottering about prompts the exclamation that it is amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a participle for lurching about unsteadily and an adjective for something stunning or amazing.

clue.text: Ignorant girl, last to argue about conflict

indicators.note: last to asks for just the final letter of the next word
about means surrounding, so the girl and the letter go round the conflict

blocks.note: Una is a girl's name
final letter of the word
a war is a conflict

explanation.surface: An ill-informed girl is the last to argue about a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaware means lacking knowledge of something, the same as being ignorant of it.

clue.text: Unmarried athlete's second vest

indicators.note: second asks for only the letter in position two of the athlete

blocks.note: single means not married
second letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bachelor runner's spare running top.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless top, what Americans call a tank top and the British a vest.

clue.text: Principal device for keeping papers together

blocks.note: first meaning: main or chief
second meaning: the bent wire fastener used to bind sheets

explanation.surface: A description of the main gadget for fastening documents.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for main or chief and a noun for the wire fastener driven through sheets.

clue.text: Stealthily pursue wading bird, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak points to the spoken form of the bird's name rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a stork is a long-legged wading bird

explanation.surface: A predator creeps up on a long-legged bird in the shallows.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in non-rhotic British speech, where both words are said the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To stalk is to follow prey or a person quietly and secretly, which is stealthy pursuit.

clue.text: Roman garment worn by knight in South Pacific islands

indicators.note: a garment worn by someone wraps around them, so the robe goes round the knight

blocks.note: the toga was the robe of Roman citizens
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight dressed in a Roman robe turns up on Pacific islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom made up of over a hundred islands in the South Pacific.
